task_instance: Triage an active connectivity failure on a macOS endpoint where a remote MCP-style service repeatedly times out: define the symptom, collect the smallest useful evidence set by running the skill's bounded built-in probes (local-link responsiveness and ping, resolver-state and DNS-query checks, destination reachability, numeric traceroute path quality, per-process live network activity, and HTTP phase timing against the affected endpoint), then produce the Incident Result report that localizes the fault domain (local-link/LAN, DNS, upstream-path, remote-service/application, or inconclusive) with observations labeled observed/inferred/unknown and a confidence level.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is an evidence-based fault-domain assessment produced by actually running macOS built-in network diagnostic commands (a bounded responsiveness sample, ICMP ping samples, a resolver-state inspection, a bounded DNS query, a numeric traceroute, a bounded per-process live network capture, and HTTP connect/TLS/first-byte phase timing). The office-assistant runtime cannot run any shell commands or code of any kind, and the host is not macOS, so none of these probes can be executed. With no probe output and no live user to paste command results, there is no genuine evidence to assess, and the run rules forbid fabricating or stubbing the probe output the skill's tools would return. The deliverable therefore cannot be produced or verified in this runtime.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md for the connectivity-triage skill. Its Fast Decision Flow and numbered steps require executing built-in diagnostic tools (a bounded network-quality responsiveness sample, ping ICMP samples to local and remote targets, a system-resolver state inspection, a bounded DNS lookup, a bounded numeric traceroute, a bounded per-process live network-activity capture, and an HTTP phase-timing request against the affected endpoint) and then interpreting their output to pick one fault-domain category with a confidence level. Every one of these is a shell command run against a live network on a macOS endpoint. The granted runtime provides only text file read/write/edit plus web fetch/search, cannot run code or commands, and is not macOS, so no probe could be run and no measured evidence collected. No command was executed. Wrote this result.json to the work directory at the path requested; no other deliverable could be created or verified.
